q: How many Shramik Special trains have been arranged by Indian Railways till the first week of June 2020, to ferry the migrants due to Covid-19?
e: Option B (Between 3000 and 4000 trains) is the correct choice. Option (B) is correct: Indian Railways ran between 3000 and 4000 Shramik Special trains till the first week of June 2020 to ferry migrant workers home during the Covid-19 lockdown. It was one of the largest mass-transportation operations by rail anywhere. Related exam fact: these specials were operated on request of state governments, with the Railways coordinating routes and schedules.

q: The commodities largely moved by Railways during the lockdown period were:
e: Foodgrains, salt, sugar, milk van — that is the right answer. Option (C) is correct: during the lockdown the commodities largely moved by Railways were foodgrains, salt, sugar and milk vans — essential supplies kept moving while most other traffic stopped. The Railways ran parcel and milk specials to maintain the food supply chain. Related exam fact: maintaining essential-commodity movement during the lockdown demonstrated the railway's role as the country's lifeline in emergencies. q: For better monitoring of big Railway projects, they have been categorized as:

options.A: Super critical, critical and throughput enhancement projects
options.B: High speed, safety and heavy haul projects
options.C: Projects with Rs.500 crores each and Rs.1000 crore each
options.D: Out of turn projects, Urgency based projects and Safety works projects

e: The correct answer is Super critical, critical and throughput enhancement projects. Option (A) is correct: for better monitoring, big railway projects are categorized as super critical, critical and throughput enhancement projects. The categorization prioritizes funding and management attention by strategic importance. Related exam fact: super-critical projects get the highest priority in fund allocation and are monitored most closely for timely completion. Notice how precisely the correct option is worded.

q: The Net Revenue projection for 2020-21 is:
e: The correct answer is Rs. 6,500 crores. Option (C) is correct: the Net Revenue projection for 2020-21 was Rs. 6,500 crores — the surplus left after meeting working expenses and appropriations to funds. Net revenue is the bottom-line surplus of railway finances for the year. Related exam fact: a healthy net revenue lets the Railways fund its Development Fund and Capital Fund from internal resources instead of borrowings.

q: Which of the following is NOT a Reserve Fund of Indian Railways as in 2019-20:
e: Option (C) is correct: Revenue Reserve Fund is NOT a reserve fund of Indian Railways — the actual reserve funds as in 2019-20 included the Depreciation Reserve Fund, Development Fund, Capital Fund, Debt Service Fund and RRSK (Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh). The Depreciation Reserve Fund is the railway fund into which appropriations are made to meet the cost of replacing assets as they wear out, keeping renewals financed.

q: Which of the following is NOT owned by Indian Railways?
e: Delhi Metro — that is the right answer. Option (A) is correct: Delhi Metro is NOT owned by Indian Railways — it belongs to the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation, a joint venture of the Government of India and the Delhi government. In contrast, Kolkata Metro is owned and operated by Indian Railways as a zone. Related exam fact: Konkan Railway Corporation is a public-sector undertaking under the Ministry of Railways, so it is within the railway family.

q: After the merger of the Railway Budget, what has been the major implication:

options.A: Railways no longer has to prepare its Annual Statement of Receipts & Expenditure
options.B: The Finance Ministry prepares the Railway Budget
options.C: Railways no longer have to pay dividend to the Government

e: The correct answer is Railways no longer have to pay dividend to the Government. Option (C) is correct: the major implication of the Railway Budget merger was that Railways no longer have to pay dividend to the Government — the capital-at-charge on which dividend was paid was wiped out from 2016-17. Railway finances became part of the General Budget with gross budgetary support. Related exam fact: the merger, effective from 2017-18, was recommended by the Bibek Debroy Committee on railway restructuring.

q: Vande Bharat Express was manufactured by:
e: The correct answer is ICF, Chennai. Option (C) is correct: the Vande Bharat Express was manufactured by the Integral Coach Factory (ICF), Chennai — India's first indigenous semi-high-speed trainset, earlier called Train 18. It was designed and built entirely in India under the Make in India initiative. Related exam fact: ICF is one of the oldest and largest coach production units of Indian Railways.
